name: Factor V Short Isoforms-Related Bleeding Disorder
aliases: Factor V Short Variant Bleeding Disorder

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Factor V Short Isoform Bleeding Disorder Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Prolonged prothrombin time (PT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) not corrected by mixing studies
Reduced Factor V activity levels specifically linked to short isoform deficiency
Identification of mutations affecting Factor V short isoforms by molecular genetic testing
Personal or family history of mucocutaneous bleeding or excessive bleeding after trauma or surgery

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prolonged PT/aPTT with reduced Factor V activity and confirmatory genetic testing identifying short isoform mutations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other coagulation factor deficiencies and inhibitors.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mucocutaneous bleeding with prolonged bleeding time
searchTerms: bleeding from skin and mucous membranes with slow clotting
mucocutaneous bleeding with prolonged bleeding time
extended bleeding in mucous membranes and skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Prolonged bleeding following minor surgical procedures

rare.symptomName: Severe anemia secondary to chronic bleeding
searchTerms: low red blood cells due to ongoing bleeding
anemia caused by frequent blood loss

laboratory: Prolonged PT and aPTT not corrected by mixing studies
Reduced Factor V activity specific to short isoforms
imaging: Imaging may reveal bleeding complications such as hemarthrosis or intracranial hemorrhage
genetic: Mutations in the F5 gene affecting short isoform expression
other: Family history of bleeding disorder consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Global reduction in Factor V activity affecting all isoforms
Different genetic mutations in F5 gene
Deficiencies in Factor VIII or IX (hemophilia A and B) with X-linked inheritance

redFlags: Unexplained prolonged bleeding after minor trauma or surgery
Severe mucocutaneous bleeding in neonates or infants
references: Orphanet: Factor V Short Isoforms-Related Bleeding Disorder, ORPHA:599519
Mannucci PM, Tuddenham EG. The hemophilias—from royal genes to gene therapy. N Engl J Med. 2001
F5 gene mutation and bleeding disorders: A review. Blood Reviews, 2023
